questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en:
Contrary to the literature, the climate change projections outlined in this paper

will cause a large reduction in temperatures in polar regions. In any case,

there is no doubt that if we do nothing, climate change

of any kind will have major effects on our daily lives.
options_hi:
Contrary to the literature, the climate change projections outlined in this paper

will cause a large reduction in temperatures in polar regions. In any case,

there is no doubt that if we do nothing, climate change

of any kind will have major effects on our daily lives.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Answer is Option B.

Explanation: In the first sentence, the phrase “contrary to the literature” shows that the statement is not a generally accepted fact, but rather a hypothetical or speculative conclusion based on projections or models. Because of this uncertainty, we use “would” instead of “will” to express a less definite, more tentative result.

So, “will cause” → “would cause”

This use of “would” indicates that the result is conditional, theoretical, or dependent on certain assumptions, which is common in academic and scientific writing.

Corrected sentence: Contrary to the literature, the climate change projections outlined in this paper would cause a large reduction in temperatures in polar regions.

In the second sentence:

…if we do nothing, climate change (of any kind) will have major effects on our daily lives.

This is a first conditional structure, used to describe a real and likely future consequence.

The correct structure is: if + present simple, will + base verb

 

  • if we do nothing → present simple ✔
  • will have major effects → future simple ✔

So, the second sentence is grammatically correct and needs no change.

While policy interventions aim to ensure equal opportunity, critics argue that superficial reforms may [---1---] existing power structures rather than dismantle them. Sustainable progress therefore demands a [---4---] commitment to equity—one that confronts systemic barriers instead of merely alleviating their visible symptoms.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [3] :

Reflexive skepticism denotes an automatic, experience-driven distrust. Given repeated disappointments, marginalized groups instinctively doubt institutional claims, making reflexive the most accurate descriptor.
WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
• Complacent implies passive satisfaction, not doubt.
• Deferential suggests respect or submission, not skepticism.
• Conciliatory implies willingness to compromise, which is not indicated.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

__________ you submit the form on time, your application will be rejected.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

__________ you submit the form on time, your application will be rejected.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option B

👉 The blank should be filled with “Unless”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Logical Polarity (Positive vs. Negative)

In conditional sentences, the choice between If and Unless depends on the "polarity" (positive or negative nature) of the condition and the result.

💢 Positive vs. Negative Breakdown

To find the right answer, we analyze the two parts of the sentence:

The Condition: "you submit the form on time" (Grammatically Positive)

The Result: "your application will be rejected" (Logically Negative)

 

✅ Logic Verification

If-Alternative: "If you do not submit... you will be rejected." (This is logical).

Unless-Equivalent: Since Unless = If + Not, the sentence becomes: "If you not submit... you will be rejected."

✅ Correct Sentence

Unless you submit the form on time, your application will be rejected.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The supervisor said to the staff, "Why did you fail to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent last week?"
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The supervisor said to the staff, "Why did you fail to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent last week?"
options_en: The supervisor asked the staff why they failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor enquired the staff that why they had failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor wanted to know why they had failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor asked the staff why had they failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
options_hi: The supervisor asked the staff why they failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor enquired the staff that why they had failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor wanted to know why they had failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
The supervisor asked the staff why had they failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The supervisor wanted to know why they had failed to update the ledger despite the repeated reminders sent the previous week.

Key Points

  • In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said to" in Direct Speech is changed into "wanted to know", "enquired (of)", or "asked".

  • In Indirect Speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech. This means the question form ("why did you fail") changes to the assertive form ("why they had failed").

  • For "Wh-" questions, the question word (Why, How, etc.) acts as the conjunction itself. Using an additional conjunction like "that" (as seen in the second option) is grammatically incorrect.

  • Tense Change: The sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Past Simple tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past Perfect tense ("had failed").

  • Time Expression: The word "last week" in Direct Speech changes to "the previous week" in Indirect Speech.

  • Pronoun Change: The second-person pronoun "you" changes according to the object of the reporting verb ("the staff"), becoming "they".

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The review panel observed that nobody present in
the briefing was less confused than the junior officers
after the complex operational plan was explained.
options_hi: The review panel observed that nobody present in
the briefing was less confused than the junior officers
after the complex operational plan was explained.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B).

Replace “than the junior officers” with “than the junior officers else”.

Rule/Concept: Use of “else” after an indefinite pronoun in comparative degree.

When a sentence begins with an indefinite pronoun like nobody, no one, nothing, anyone, and a comparative degree is used, “else” is mandatory to exclude the person or group already mentioned and to avoid self-comparison.

Application to the Given Question - “The review panel observed that nobody present in the briefing was less confused than the junior officers …”

Here, “nobody” is an indefinite pronoun.

Without “else”, the sentence illogically compares nobody with the same group already included.

Adding “else” clearly means excluding the junior officers from the comparison.

Corrected Sentence - The review panel observed that nobody present in the briefing was less confused than the junior officers else after the complex operational plan was explained.

More Examples for Clarity -

There is no one else wiser than him in the unit.

Nothing else is more important than discipline in the forces.

Nobody else was braver than the soldier during the mission.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Indefinite pronoun + comparative → ELSE is compulsory

Look for words like nobody, no one, nothing, anyone.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The motivational workshop conducted by the manager last
week was truly inspiring for the new recruits, who
feeling inspired by the session and actively participated in it.
options_hi: The motivational workshop conducted by the manager last
Week was truly inspiring for the new recruits, who
feeling inspired by the session and actively participated in it.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) – Replace “feeling inspired” with “felt inspired”.

Rule / Concept: Participial Adjectives: “-ing” vs “-ed”

Present Participle (-ing): Describes the cause of a feeling (active).

Past Participle (-ed): Describes the receiver of a feeling (passive/state).

Using the wrong participle creates a grammatical error and changes the meaning of the sentence.

Application to the Given Question -

Here, “who feeling inspired” is in the wrong form. The recruits are the receiver of inspiration, so the past participle “felt inspired” must be used.

Corrected Sentence - The motivational workshop conducted by the senior manager last week was truly inspiring for the new recruits, who felt inspired by the sessions and actively participated in every activity.

More Examples for Clarity -

The movie was boring, so the audience felt bored.

The thrilling roller coaster ride left the children excited.

The frightening dog scared the little girl, leaving her frightened.

Incorrect Usage -

The students were exciting about the new project.

The teacher was interested in the lecture, feeling interested.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

"The audience, after witnessing the breathtaking finale of the opera, _________ now returning to their respective homes using different modes of transportation."
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

"The audience, after witnessing the breathtaking finale of the opera, _________ now returning to their respective homes using different modes of transportation."
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B)

The plural verb "are" is required here because the members of the audience are acting as individuals.

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns (The Split vs. The Unit)

United Action (Singular): When the group acts as a single, unanimous body, use a Singular Verb.

Individual Action (Plural): When the members are acting separately, moving in different directions, or have differing opinions, use a Plural Verb.

Logic Breakdown:

The Context Clues: The sentence mentions "their respective homes" and "different modes of transportation."

The Logic: Since the audience members are going to different homes in different cars/buses, they are no longer acting as one giant block. They are acting as hundreds of individuals.

The Pronoun Check: Notice the use of the plural possessive pronoun "their" in the sentence. This is a massive hint that the verb must also be plural (are).

Correct Sentence: The audience... are now returning to their respective homes...

While individuals may profess strong moral beliefs, real commitment becomes evident when actions involve [--1---] consequences rather than symbolic gestures. In professional environments, ethical lapses are frequently justified as pragmatic compromises, yet such reasoning can gradually [-----2----] moral accountability. Over time, repeated rationalization of minor transgressions fosters a climate of [----3---] indifference, where wrongdoing is normalized rather than questioned. Scholars therefore argue that ethical integrity must be sustained through a [---4----] adherence to values, independent of external reward or recognition.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [3] :

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C).

Remove “yourself”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Verbs that are Inherent Reflexive –

In English, certain verbs naturally imply that the action is being done to the subject. Because the "self" is already understood within the meaning of the verb, adding a reflexive pronoun (myself, yourself, himself, etc.) is considered redundant (unnecessary repetition)

REMEMBER THE LIST : Don’t use reflexive pronoun after these verbs:- Keep, Remain, Concentrate, Stop, Turn, Qualify, Bathe, Move, Rest, Hide etc.

Application to the Given Question- The verb "concentrate" already means to focus one's own mind. Adding "yourself" after it creates a grammatical redundancy.

Corrected Sentence - In order to succeed in the exam, you must concentrate on your studies.

to be the dean of the university.

options_hi: The woman, whom I assumed
was a guest lecturer, turned out
to be the dean of the university.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A).

Replace “whom” with “who”.

Rule / Concept: The "Who" vs. "Whom" Subject Test

ALWAYS CHECK NO OF SUBJECT= NO OF VERB

This is one of the most deceptive rules in English because of parenthetical phrases (interrupters) like "I assumed," "I thought," or "they believed."

In this sentence, even though "whom" follows the verb "assumed," it is actually the subject of the verb "was" in the next clause

Corrected Sentence -The woman, who I assumed was a guest lecturer, turned out to be the dean of the university.

Rule / Concept: Incorrect Comparison (Faulty Comparison)

A faulty comparison occurs when two non-comparable things are compared. Only like things (same category) should be compared. Here, literacy rate of Kerala (a quantity) is correctly compared to Tamil Nadu (a state). Both sides of the comparison must refer to the same type of entity, i.e., literacy rate of Kerala vs literacy rate of Tamil Nadu.

More Examples for Clarity -

The GDP growth of India is higher than the GDP growth of China this year.

The unemployment rate in Maharashtra is worse than the unemployment rate in Gujarat.

The rainfall in Bihar is lower than the rainfall in Uttar Pradesh this monsoon.

Incorrect Usage -

My height is more than India.

The price of gold is higher than Delhi.

questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The coach told the team that if they won that match, he would give them a week's holiday.

Key Points

  • Indirect Speech: The reporting verb "said to" changes to "told" because it is followed by an object ("the team").

  • Key Conversions:

    • "If you win the match" becomes "If they won that match": The conditional clause in Simple Present ("win") is changed to Simple Past ("won") to match the indirect speech timeline.

    • "this" becomes "that": The demonstrative "this" changes to "that" in indirect speech.

    • "I will give" becomes "he would give": The first-person pronoun "I" changes to "he" (referring to the coach), and the future "will" changes to its past form "would".

  • Pronoun Change: The second-person pronoun "you" refers to the "team" (plural), so it changes to "they" (subject) and "them" (object) in Indirect Speech.

  • Structural Integrity: Option C is the only one that correctly applies the backshift to both the conditional "if" clause and the main clause while maintaining correct pronoun agreement.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “find” with “founded”.

📌 Rule / Concept: (Find vs. Found)

The confusion arises because the Past Tense (V2) of 'Find' is 'Found', but 'Found' is also a separate Base Verb (V1) meaning to establish.

Find (V1) – Found (V2) – Found (V3): To discover something that exists.

Found (V1) – Founded (V2) – Founded (V3): To establish, set up, or lay the groundwork for an organization or institution.

In Passive Voice (was/were + V3), we must choose the correct V3 form based on the intended meaning (discovery vs. establishment).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The sentence refers to the establishment of a non-profit organization. Therefore, we need the Past Participle (V3) of the verb Found (to establish), which is Founded. The word "find" is the base form for discovery and is grammatically incorrect after the auxiliary verb "was" in this context.

Corrected Sentence - The non-profit organization was founded by a group of activists dedicated to environmental conservation.

While individuals may profess strong moral beliefs, real commitment becomes evident when actions involve [--1---] consequences rather than symbolic gestures. Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

• Hypothetical refers to imagined situations, not real action.
• Ornamental implies decorative or showy gestures, which the sentence rejects.

📌 Rule / Concept: Born vs. Borne

Both words are past participles of the verb bear, but they are used in distinct contexts:

Born: Used exclusively in the context of birth (e.g., "He was born in 1990"). In the passive voice, it is used only when not followed by the word "by".

Borne: This is the versatile past participle used for all other meanings of bear—such as to carry, to support, to endure, or to produce. It is also used in the passive voice when followed by "by," even in the context of birth (though rare in modern exams).

VERB FORM: Bear bore borne/born
